body.target_estimand: \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\), where \(\tau_P\) is the unique continuous Hölder representative of the conditional causal contrast

sampling_model.units: The records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent under each component law; each diagnostic sample mixture retains one shared nuisance-sign vector across all records.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator is supplied. The finite pair score averages out nuisance signs through an exact core-cell second moment and normalizes every occupied cell by its realized ordered-pair count.

Section 3 constructs pure-private simple-hypothesis tests from clamped one-record log-likelihood ratios.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad lower bounds through mixture couplings and expected Hamming distance.
Section 4.1, Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16 give a pure-private T-mechanism whose generic finite-cover control contains \(\log|\mathcal P_\eta|\).
The paper constructs central-private U-statistic estimators using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 give pure-private finite-hypothesis and cover-based selection with costs proportional to \(\log m\) and \(\log|\mathcal C_\alpha|\).
The paper provides composition-based differentially private CATE meta-learners without a sharp pure-private pointwise Hölder minimax frontier.
Theorems 1 and 3 give observational Neyman-orthogonal CATE releases under approximate \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-differential privacy using Gaussian vector or Gaussian-process perturbations.

body.tldr: Unknown propensity can make separated pointwise CATE fibers have identical one-record nuisance mixtures while leaving an exact two-record signal. On a smooth signed family inside the unchanged exact-uniform Hölder class, an occupancy-normalized pair score removes the nuisance sign on every core, has replacement sensitivity at most four, and yields a finite pure-private test and two-point estimator with error \(C\exp(-ckp_2a^2b^2)+C\exp(-c\epsilon kp_2ab)\), without a nuisance-cardinality logarithm. A fully specified quantized experiment gives exact total-variation, Bayes-risk, and privacy calculations. Within the two-scale geometry \(q<\gamma\) and sparse-occupancy regime, the separation is \(\max\{r_{\mathrm{pair}},r_F\}\) on this signed experiment; the full-class frontier remains an open score-construction question stated through an explicit weighted shell functional.

project_justification.gap: Simple private tests use additive one-record likelihood increments, while generic private selection and T-mechanisms control finite covers through cardinality terms. The coupled CATE fibers here have intersecting one-record convex hulls, and the published results do not supply a nuisance-independent second-order score certificate for them.
project_justification.niche: A higher-order private test can use a signal common to every nuisance profile only when two observations occupy the same public localization cell. Realized occupancy normalization preserves constant replacement sensitivity and the \(n^2\epsilon\) pair-information balance.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs and audits the pair test on a legal smooth two-fiber family, proves an explicit pure-private test and risk bound, gives an exact finite experiment, and reduces the full-class lift to one precisely defined weighted shell functional.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024), Theorems 1--2 and Section 5, define the nonprivate Hölder pointwise-CATE benchmark and localized higher-order geometry; those results inform the smooth family but are not claimed as private comparators. Canonne et al. (2019), Section 3, construct optimal private simple tests from clamped one-record likelihood ratios; Theorem 1 identifies a composite-fiber convex-hull obstruction to that representation. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021) provide central-private mixture converses through Hamming transport, informing the interpretation of the pair radius rather than its upper test. Asi et al. (2024), Section 4.1, Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16, control their pure-private T-mechanism over finite total-variation covers with \(\log|\mathcal P_\eta|\); the signed-family theorem avoids catalogue selection through a common pair orientation but does not claim a generic strengthening of their result. Bun et al. (2021), Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, give pure-private hypothesis and cover selection with \(\log m\) and \(\log|\mathcal C_\alpha|\) costs; those bounds are informed-by comparators rather than the same composite testing task. Chaudhuri et al. (2024) stabilize private U-statistics with local Hájek projections, while the exact core normalization and shared causal second moment here are problem-specific. Niu et al. (2022) give private CATE meta-learners without a pure-private pointwise Hölder frontier. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025), Theorems 1 and 3, give observational Neyman-orthogonal finite and functional CATE releases using Gaussian perturbations under approximate \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-privacy; they neither analyze pure privacy nor provide a shared-mixture pair test.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The early-kill experiment used \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\), \(n=2\), \(a=b=2/25\), and \(\epsilon=1\). For \(k=1,\ldots,8\), the finite nonprivate test and the pure-private linear program were solved on all \((4k)^2\) ordered datasets, with every one-record replacement edge imposed. The total variation was exactly \(0.0256/k\); the optimal private error equaled \(\{1-(0.0256/k)\tanh(1/2)\}/2\); randomized response attained that value; and the exhaustive maximum neighboring log-ratio was one. The exact symmetry formula was then checked through \(k=12\). The constant-mixture subexperiment verified convex-hull collision, while the shared-sign subexperiment verified the pair signal. The persistent loss was the collision probability \(1/k\), not a nuisance-entropy penalty. These finite checks do not prove the full-class lifting question, and the theorem deliberately remains in the sparse-occupancy regime \(nv\le c_0\); dense occupancy or arbitrary least-favorable priors may require a different concentration or stabilization argument.
body.honest_scope: The formal contribution is the exact-uniform smooth signed two-fiber family, its one-record convex-hull obstruction, the sparse-occupancy pure-private pair test, and a completely specified finite audit. The pair-radius specialization is restricted to the new two-scale geometry \(q<\gamma\) and \(nv\le c_0\); it makes no rate claim for \(q\ge\gamma\) or dense occupancy. It does not establish the full-class private minimax frontier. That frontier appears only as Open-ended Question 1 through a second-order least-favorable-mixture handle and the explicit functional \(\mathfrak W_r\). For \(k=1\) and \(\lambda=(\lambda_1)\), two independent records \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)\sim P_{s,(\lambda_1)}\), with \(U_i=2A_i-1\), \(V_i=2Y_i-1\), and \(Z_{12}=(U_1V_2+V_1U_2)/2\), obey \(\mathbb E_{P_{s,(\lambda_1)}^{\otimes2}}[Z_{12}\mid X_1,X_2\in C_1]=4sab\).
